examples.en: My throat stung, so I drank a lot of water.
The arm where I got the shot still stings.
Shampoo got in my eyes and they stung.

examples.ko: 약을 바르면 조금 따끔거릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: It may sting a little when you apply the medicine.
My sunburned skin stings, what should I do?
The mosquito bite stung and then started to itch.

explain: '따끔하다'는 한 번 찌르는 듯 짧게 아플 때 많이 쓰고, '따끔거리다'는 그 느낌이 계속 되풀이될 때 써요. 목, 눈, 상처, 피부처럼 쓰라린 곳에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '따끔하다' is often used for a brief prick, while '따끔거리다' is used when that stinging feeling keeps repeating. It fits sore spots like the throat, eyes, wounds and skin.

examples.ko: 아기를 낳고 한 달 동안 몸조리를 했어요.
examples.en: After giving birth, I rested and recovered for a month.

examples.ko: 감기 심하게 걸렸다면서요? 푹 쉬고 몸조리 잘하세요.
examples.en: I heard you caught a bad cold. Rest well and take care of yourself.
After surgery, you have to rest and recover at home.
My mom came to help me with my recovery.
If you don't take care of yourself during recovery, you'll suffer later.
After leaving the hospital, I recovered at my country house.

explain: 아프거나 아기를 낳은 뒤에 쉬면서 건강을 되찾는 것이에요. 아픈 사람에게 '몸조리 잘하세요'라고 하면 '푹 쉬고 잘 회복하세요'라는 인사말이 돼요. 출산 후에는 '산후조리'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means resting and regaining your health after an illness or childbirth. Telling a sick person '몸조리 잘하세요' works as a greeting meaning 'rest well and recover'. After childbirth it is also called '산후조리'.

examples.en: This sweater can only be hand-washed.
Lukewarm water is best for hand-washing.
The clothing label says hand wash.
If you hand-wash, clothes get less damaged.
The washing machine has a hand-wash cycle.
After hand-washing, dry it in the shade.

explain: 세탁기를 쓰는 '기계 세탁'과 반대되는 말이에요. 옷 라벨이나 세탁 설명에서 많이 보고, 대화에서는 '손빨래'라고도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of machine washing. You see it on clothing labels and in laundry instructions, and in conversation people often say '손빨래' too.

examples.en: I went to the hospital to get a flu shot.
The flu spread widely this winter.

examples.ko: 아이가 인플루엔자에 걸려서 학교에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: My child caught the flu and couldn't go to school.
My fever was so high that I thought it was the flu.
I rested for a week because of the flu.
The flu test result will come out tomorrow.

explain: 일상에서는 '독감'이라는 말을 훨씬 많이 쓰고, 인플루엔자는 병원이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 그냥 '감기'와 달리 열이 높고 몸이 많이 아파요. '독감에 걸리다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: In daily life people say 독감 much more often; 인플루엔자 is used at hospitals and in the news. Unlike a plain 감기 (cold), it brings a high fever and body aches. You say 독감에 걸리다 for catching it.

examples.en: The spring rain softly moistened the earth all night.

examples.ko: 피부를 촉촉이 유지하려고 물을 많이 마셔요.
examples.en: I drink a lot of water to keep my skin moist.
Morning dew formed softly on the blades of grass.

examples.ko: 빗속을 걷다 보니 머리가 촉촉이 젖었어요.
examples.en: After walking in the rain, my hair got damp.
My eyes grew moist while watching the movie.

examples.ko: 마른 화분에 물을 주어 흙을 촉촉이 적셨어요.
examples.en: I watered the dry flowerpot and moistened the soil.

explain: 조금 젖어서 부드럽고 눈에 띄게 습기가 있는 모양을 말해요. '적시다, 젖다, 맺히다' 같은 동사와 같이 자주 나와요. 말할 때는 '촉촉하게'도 같은 뜻으로 자연스럽게 써요.
explain_en: It describes something lightly wet, soft and visibly damp. It often appears with verbs like '적시다', '젖다' and '맺히다'. In speech, '촉촉하게' is also a natural way to say the same thing.
